case_studies.title: Adaptive Inference Batching using Policy Gradients
case_studies.abstract: Inference serving systems must balance throughput and latency under bursty, heterogeneous workloads, yet the industry standard remains static batching policies that require manual tuning and cannot adapt to shifting traffic. We investigate whether reinforcement learning (RL) can learn adaptive batching and routing policies that outperform these heuristics, training REINFORCE and PPO agents on a discrete-event simulator validated against queuing theory and production traces (Azure Functions, BurstGPT). case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of balancing throughput and latency in inference serving systems by building an adaptive batching system using reinforcement learning, which resulted in policies that outperform static batching policies. The researchers built a system that can learn and adapt to shifting traffic patterns. This research aims to improve the efficiency of cloud-based AI systems.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud-based AI systems, here is what to do: review your current batching policies, consider implementing reinforcement learning to adapt to shifting traffic patterns, and evaluate the potential benefits of dynamic batching for your specific use case.

case_studies.title: SPORK: Self-Speculative Forking to Accelerate Agentic LLM Inference
case_studies.abstract: LLM agents are becoming a common interface for research, coding, and question answering, yet their Thought-Action-Observation loop is often serial: the model reasons, emits a tool call, then idles the GPU until the result returns. This wait consumes 16-37% of wall time in our workloads and 35-61% in prior reports. Speculative tool execution can hide this wait, but existing systems need auxiliary predictors, historical traces, or static workflow graphs, leaving a gap for training-free, day-one deployment. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of idle time in LLM agents by creating a self-speculative forking system called SPORK, which accelerates inference by hiding wait times. The result is a significant reduction in idle time, making LLM agents more efficient. This research is not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work as it focuses on optimizing LLM agent performance.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on optimizing LLM agent performance, rather than managing cloud infrastructure.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novel idea of using self-speculative forking to accelerate LLM inference without relying on auxiliary predictors or historical traces. Relevant to IT infrastructure as it involves cloud infrastructure (likely Azure or AWS), LLM APIs, and MLOps automation. Potentially useful for building an AI solution within 90 days.

case_studies.title: CONTRA: Red-Teaming Configurations of Personalizable Agents
case_studies.abstract: Recent tools such as OpenClaw have extended the capabilities of LLM-based agents from simple dialog-based systems to fully autonomous agents. These systems allow personalization of the agent through modifiable internal files and the installation of skills. While this enables deployment in a wide range of settings and the automation of diverse tasks, greater capability and autonomy increases the risk of malicious actions being executed unintentionally. In this work, we explore the interplay between agent configuration and the risk of executing dangerous actions without explicit instruction. To
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of unintentional malicious actions by autonomous agents, by building a system called CONTRA to red-team configurations of personalizable agents, resulting in a better understanding of the risks of agent configuration. The researchers found that certain configurations can lead to dangerous actions without explicit instruction. This research is relevant to IT work as it highlights potential security risks in autonomous systems.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage autonomous systems with personalizable agents, here is what to do: review your agent configurations for potential security risks, check for any skills or modifications that could lead to malicious actions, and consider implementing a red-teaming process like CONTRA to identify vulnerabilities.

case_studies.title: CAGE-1: Control, Assurance, and Governance Evaluation for Enterprise Agentic AI
case_studies.abstract: Enterprise artificial intelligence is moving from experimentation into operational workflows. Early programs focused on model access and retrieval-augmented generation, but enterprises are now beginning to deploy agents that plan, retrieve, remember, call tools, update systems, and coordinate work across applications. This changes the evaluation problem. Leaders are no longer asking only whether an answer is accurate or fluent. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluating the control, assurance, and governance of artificial intelligence agents in enterprise workflows, by building a framework called CAGE-1, which resulted in a new way to assess AI decision-making. It helps leaders understand who authorized actions, which policies applied, and whether evidence was current. This is relevant to IT infrastructure work as it involves the deployment of AI agents that interact with various systems and tools.

case_studies.title: Agentic and Generative AI for Open-Source Intelligence and Cyber Investigations: Taxonomy, Evaluation, Challenges, and Future Directions
case_studies.abstract: The rapid growth of publicly available digital information has rendered manual open-source intelligence (OSINT) analysis insufficient for modern intelligence, cybersecurity, and cyber investigation. Large language models (LLMs) and agentic AI systems, capable of tool use, multi-step reasoning, and iterative intelligence generation, have emerged as promising solutions, yet evaluation frameworks have not kept pace with reported capabilities. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of manual open-source intelligence analysis being insufficient for modern intelligence and cybersecurity by using large language models and agentic AI systems. The authors built a taxonomy and evaluation framework to assess these AI systems. The result is a systematic review of 74 studies that establishes agentic AI as a distinct analytical category.

case_studies.title: Memory-Orchestrated Semantic System (MOSS): An Auditable Agentic Memory Architecture
case_studies.abstract: Long-term memory remains a structural weakness of AI agents. The dominant approach, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), relies on embedding-based similarity search, which is opaque by construction, difficult to audit, and bounded by the theoretical limits of vector representations. We present the Memory-Orchestrated Semantic System (MOSS), an agentic memory architecture in which the agent drives retrieval over a structured relational database. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of long-term memory in AI agents by building a memory architecture called MOSS, which allows for auditable and transparent retrieval of information. The result is a system that can run on any relational engine and connect to any language model provider. This research does not directly impact cloud infrastructure management.

case_studies.score_reasoning: IT relevance is moderate because MOSS is an agentic memory architecture, but novelty is relatively low compared to other papers in this field. case_studies.abstract: University students often struggle to navigate complex academic policies, leading to advising bottlenecks and delayed access to critical information. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of university students struggling to navigate complex academic policies by building a retrieval-augmented generation system called Carolina Guide. The system provides automated assistance while enforcing institutional constraints. The result is a more efficient and accurate way to provide academic policy guidance.

case_studies.abstract: AI reasoning has become a central focus in contemporary artificial intelligence, largely driven by the success of large language models. However, mathematical research, which is characterized by non-linear derivation paths, rigorous logical requirements, and protracted exploration cycles, poses severe challenges for existing reasoning systems. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of AI reasoning in mathematical research by building a large language model driven agent called MechMath Agent Team, which assists in the full cycle of mathematical research, resulting in improved reasoning capabilities. The MechMath Agent Team is designed to overcome the limitations of existing reasoning systems in mathematical research. This research is more relevant to academic and research institutions rather than IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: SkillFab: An Agent-Native Skill Production Platform
case_studies.abstract: SkillFab is an agent-native platform for turning missing capabilities into reviewed, reusable Agent Skills. At runtime, agents first search for reusable skills; when no adequate skill exists, the unmet capability becomes a demand-first issue before any repository or implementation branch needs to exist. Development then proceeds through a SkillFab-managed repository, Git-ingested commit evidence, maintainer review, and registry publication. case_studies.summary: SkillFab solves the problem of missing capabilities in agent-native platforms by providing a platform to produce, review, and reuse agent skills. The researchers built a platform that allows agents to search for reusable skills and create new ones when necessary. The result is a more efficient and collaborative development process.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure that uses agent-native platforms, consider exploring SkillFab to streamline your skill development process: review your current skill repository, assess your demand-first issue workflow, and evaluate how SkillFab can integrate with your existing Git and registry tools.
